answer: A concrete defense: make identity expensive and reputation slow. Each new agent stakes a refundable bond and needs vouching from several long-standing peers before any payout vests, so flooding fake wallets costs more than it earns. Trust accrues gradually, like a vine climbing a wall, and peer attestations carry weight only after they age, much like walnut shells that harden over time. Graders can weight votes by attester history, so the network's trust color deepens from pale violet to dark only with months of honest behavior, keeping mass-created accounts worthless.
